title: Sales & CS aggregator and quick-scope playbook for enterprise asks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Sales and Customer Success frequently surface enterprise feature requests (non-bug) that arrive as product ideas, compliance asks, and integration needs. Currently those asks are tracked in ad-hoc notes, Slack threads, and individual spreadsheets which creates duplicate entries, inconsistent context, and slow prioritization loops. Objective: Create a lightweight aggregator + quick-scope playbook that Sales/CS can use to submit, consolidate, and do an initial triage of enterprise feature requests so PMs can make faster prioritization decisions. Outcomes: 1) single source-of-truth intake form for Sales/CS; 2) deterministic triage rubric that produces a score and recommended next step (backlog, discovery, roadmap candidate, escalate); 3) weekly review cadence with clear ownership and SLAs for initial response.
acceptance_criteria: A templated intake form exists (Confluence + Link to Google Form/Sheets) and is discoverable by Sales/CS
Submitted requests are consolidated into a canonical sheet and deduped automatically or manually within 48 hours
Each submission receives an initial triage score within 5 business days and a recommended next step
PMs can filter/segment asks by impact, revenue TMV, technical risk, and compliance needs
Playbook includes a runbook for urgent compliance/security asks with >24h escalation path
triage_rubric: Score components (0-5 each): Business Impact (customers affected & revenue potential), Urgency (contract or go-live dates), Strategic Fit (alignment with roadmap thesis), Technical Effort (estimated engineering story points), Data/Security/Compliance Risk. Weighting: Business Impact x3, Urgency x2, Strategic Fit x2, Technical Effort negative weight -1, Compliance Risk x3. Score bands: 30+ -> Roadmap candidate; 18-29 -> Discovery/PM deep-dive; 10-17 -> Backlog; <10 -> Monitor/decline.
initial_scoping_template: Required fields for intake: 1) Customer name & ACV; 2) Short summary of ask (2-3 bullets); 3) Business/contract driver and go-live date; 4) Expected users & traffic estimate; 5) Data or compliance constraints (KMS, audit logs, VPC, retention); 6) Suggested priority (sales/CS) and any demo materials; 7) Links to customer emails, contracts, or security questionnaires; 8) Sales rep and CS owner contact info; 9) Any known dependencies (third-party integrations, infra).
